title: Fernando Henrique Cardoso begins his second term as president of Brazil.
text: Fernando Henrique Cardoso, also known by his initials FHC (Brazilian Portuguese: ), is a Brazilian sociologist, professor, and politician who served as the 34th president of Brazil from 1 January 1995 to 1 January 2003. He was the first Brazilian president to be reelected for a subsequent term.

title: Central Station by Walter Salles, wins the Golden Globe Award for Best Foreign Language Film.
text: Walter Moreira Salles Júnior is a Brazilian filmmaker. A major figure of the Resumption Cinema in Brazil, Salles is widely regarded as one of the greatest filmmakers in Brazilian cinema.

title: Antônio Carlos Magalhães (PFL/BA) and Michel Temer (PMDB/SP) are re-elected, respectively, as presidents of the Federal Senate and the Chamber of Deputies.
text: Antônio Carlos Peixoto de Magalhães, commonly known as Antônio Carlos Magalhães or by his initials ACM, was a Brazilian physician, businessman, and politician, who served three times as both senator and governor of Bahia. He is best known for his influence as a national power broker, through his political machine that dominated his state's politics and national media.

title: A blackout affects the Federal District, as well as ten states in the South, Southeast, and Central-West regions.
text: The 1999 Southern Brazil blackout was a widespread power outage that started in Brazil on 11 March 1999. The blackout involved São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, Minas Gerais, Goiás, Mato Grosso, Mato Grosso do Sul and Rio Grande do Sul, affecting an estimated 75 to 97 million people.

title: After 94 days, the kidnapping of Wellington Camargo (brother of the country duo Zezé di Camargo & Luciano) ends. Camargo was found in a bush on the side of a road in Guapó and the kidnappers were arrested.
text: Zezé Di Camargo & Luciano are a famous Brazilian sertanejo/pop/country duo. The two brothers were born in Pirenópolis, Goiás.

title: The newspaper Agora São Paulo is launched to replace Folha da Tarde.
text: Agora São Paulo was a Brazilian newspaper published by Grupo Folha which also owns the broadsheet Folha de S.Paulo. It was launched in 1999 to replace Folha da Tarde.

title: In São José dos Campos, 345 prisoners escape from Putim prison through the front gate.
text: Putim prison is a prison in São José dos Campos, Brazil.

title: Brazil defeats Uruguay 3-0, earning their sixth Copa América championship.
text: The 1999 Copa América final was the final match of the 1999 Copa América. It was held on 18 July 1999, in Asunción.

title: Francisco de Assis Pereira, "The Park Maniac", is sentenced to 121 years in prison for the death of ten women in the State Park, in São Paulo.
text: Francisco de Assis Pereira, also known as "O Maníaco do Parque" ("The Park Maniac"), is a Brazilian serial killer. He was arrested in 1998 for the rape and murder of 11 women and for assaulting nine others in a São Paulo park.

title: Mateus da Costa Meira, a 24-year old medical student, kills 3 people in a theater with a submachine gun.
text: On November 3, 1999, a mass shooting occurred inside a movie theater at the Morumbi shopping mall in São Paulo, Brazil. The perpetrator, Mateus da Costa Meira, then a 24-year-old medical student, killed three people and injured four others inside the theater.

title: Unsuccessful launch of VLS-1 V02 occurs.
text: VLS-1 V02 was the second flight of the VLS-1 rocket on December 11, 1999, from the Alcântara Launch Center, with the objective of placing the SACI-2 microsatellite in LEO. The rocket was remotely destroyed 3 minutes after launch.
